result.scientific_strategy:
## e88f7b9e-b5cb-4f9b-86c6-4115ca3a0f2b / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The human objective is at least 98% official episode success. The fresh PPO baseline learned substantial reach-and-hold behavior, but checkpoint-100352 reached 96% on each of the seed-7500 and seed-7700 disjoint research panels; its 98% task-reference result is selection-contaminated. It remains the strongest measured lineage. The full-support continuation reached 97.5% on seed 7900, tied the incumbent on every episode, and did not demonstrate a radial-support improvement. On the geometry-bearing task-reference panel, both lineages reached 98% and shared three reach failures at inner radii from 6.7 to 9.9 cm and angles from -116 to -128 degrees; the incumbent alone failed one additional target at -125 degrees and the full-support lineage alone failed one at -155 degrees and 18.2 cm. The residual deficit is therefore concentrated in reach behavior for a negative-angle sector, while the current development evidence remains below or selection-contaminated relative to the official objective.

**Lessons and limits:** Training success in the changed-radius run reached 1.0 at checkpoint-105472, then declined to 0.94 by checkpoint-120832; both measured checkpoints scored 97.5%, so this proxy decline did not translate into a task difference on seed 7900. The seed-7500, seed-7700, and seed-7900 research panels are disjoint and directly comparable, while task-reference-v1 is fixed and selection-contaminated. The research evaluator emits no target geometry, so it cannot test a geometry-specific mechanism. In the geometry-bearing artifacts, all five residual failures truncated at 500 steps with final distance just above the 1 cm threshold; they were reach failures rather than observed hold interruptions. The full-support policy fixed one incumbent failure but introduced a different negative-angle failure, so radial coverage alone is not a sufficient explanation. Training logs and proxy success do not reliably identify task superiority.

**Open questions:** Whether emphasizing the observed negative-angle sector improves reach success without creating failures elsewhere remains unresolved. The standing policy's official readiness remains uncertain because the best disjoint development result is 97.5% and the official benchmark has not been run. The contribution of learning-process variance, and the possibility of a hold-stability deficit outside the observed geometry-bearing failures, also remain uncertain; these are recorded uncertainties rather than prescribed actions.
